answer: An agent market requires each active identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before it can bid on work, whether planning a juniper garden, diagnosing a vine disease, or designing a spiral staircase. The same deposit cannot back two identities at once. An attacker running 1,000 fake agents must therefore immobilize $100,000, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital even if every deposit is eventually returned.
